7_8_hexagon_ca_vr.description: hex_cell(t+1) = life_rule(6_neighbors) stacked vertically — terrain from time
7_8_hexagon_ca_vr.name: 7_8_hexagon_ca_vr

CA_sphere.description: vertex(t+1) = evolve(mode, neighbors) where mode in {CA, random_walk, hill_seeking}
CA_sphere.name: CA_sphere

CellularAutomata3DStacked.description: layer(n+1) = life_rules(layer(n)) with outward→upward phase transition
CellularAutomata3DStacked.name: CellularAutomata3DStacked

CellularAutomata3DTree.description: square_layer(n) → ca_prune(edge, isolation, random) → tree silhouette
CellularAutomata3DTree.name: CellularAutomata3DTree

CrosswayCA.description: Each row obeys a different Wolfram rule number. Where rule regimes collide at row boundaries, interference patterns emerge — moire-like zones of order in the chaos. Every 10 turns all rules re-randomize and the entire pattern language shifts. A crossroads of computational grammars where the boundaries become the most interesting places.
CrosswayCA.qfep_connection: Critical lambda — each row is a different lambda value (rule number). The boundaries between rows are the edges of chaos, where different computational regimes interfere and produce emergent structure.
CrosswayCA.capacity: SEE that when different rules collide, the boundaries between them produce more complexity than either rule alone
interactions: observe rule collisions at row boundaries
CrosswayCA.name: CrosswayCA

ca_growth_network.description: Network structure that grows using cellular automata rules, forming organic branching patterns through local neighbor interactions.
ca_growth_network.name: CA Growth Network

ca_screen.description: Screen display that renders live cellular-automata patterns — rule outputs visualised on a flat panel as the simulation runs.
ca_screen.name: CA Screen

ca_showcase.description: A collection of various cellular automata demonstrations.
ca_showcase.name: CA Showcase
ca_showcase.qfep_connection: Survey of CA behavior classes — each class maps to a λ value. Class I (death) = λ=0, Class II (static) = low λ, Class IV (complex) = λ≈0.4, Class III (chaotic) = λ→1. The full spectrum rendered.

ca_sphere.description: Cellular Automata on a sphere surface.
ca_sphere.name: CA Sphere

crack_propagation_ca.description: Simulation of crack propagation in materials.
crack_propagation_ca.name: Crack Propagation CA

decaying_bridge.description: A bridge that decays when stepped on.
decaying_bridge.name: Decaying Bridge

disease_spread_ca.description: SIR model simulation of disease spread.
disease_spread_ca.name: Disease Spread CA
disease_spread_ca.qfep_connection: SIR epidemic dynamics as entropy propagation — infection spreads E(S) through a network, recovery restores local F. The transmission rate IS λ: how fast disorder propagates through structure.

elementary_ca_vr.description: 1D Elementary Cellular Automata in VR (Rule 30, etc).
elementary_ca_vr.name: Elementary CA VR
elementary_ca_vr.qfep_connection: Wolfram's 256 rules as a complete λ-spectrum. Rule 30 produces chaos from order, Rule 110 is Turing-complete at the edge of chaos — the simplest system that can compute anything.

game_of_life_oop_vr.description: Object-Oriented Game of Life in VR.
game_of_life_oop_vr.name: Game of Life OOP VR

game_of_life_vr.description: Conway's Game of Life in VR.
game_of_life_vr.name: Game of Life VR
game_of_life_vr.qfep_connection: Emergent gliders and oscillators are persistent low-F structures surviving in high-E(S) space. Life exists at Langton's λ ≈ 0.27 — just below the edge of chaos, where complex computation emerges from two rules.

hexagon_ca_vr.description: Cellular Automata on a hexagonal grid.
hexagon_ca_vr.name: Hexagon CA VR

hexagon_cave_vr.description: Hexagonal CA generating a cave-like structure with varying radius.
hexagon_cave_vr.name: Hexagon Cave VR

lattice_gas_automata.description: Fluid dynamics simulation using Lattice Gas Automata.
lattice_gas_automata.name: Lattice Gas Automata
lattice_gas_automata.qfep_connection: Discrete particles on a lattice reproducing continuous fluid dynamics — microscopic F (collision rules) generates macroscopic E(S) (turbulence, flow). The Navier-Stokes equations emerge from local interactions.

lenia_continuous.description: Continuous cellular automaton (Lenia) — smooth lifelike organisms emerge from a ring-shaped kernel, bell-curve growth function, and continuous [0,1] states. The 'wow' artifact for cellular automata: watch amorphous blobs self-organize into gliding, pulsing creatures on a glowing floor display.
lenia_continuous.name: Lenia Continuous
lenia_continuous.qfep_connection: Continuous CA with smooth λ-variation. Creatures self-maintain through continuous F-minimization — they persist by predicting their own next state. Lenia lives at the edge of chaos in continuous space.

line_network_ca.description: Base class visualization for line-based cellular automata.
line_network_ca.name: Line Network CA

pulsing_ca.description: Base class visualization for pulsing sphere cellular automata.
pulsing_ca.name: Pulsing CA

rule_30_110.name: Rule 30/110
rule_30_110.qfep_connection: Rule 30: deterministic chaos (high λ, unpredictable from initial conditions). Rule 110: Turing-complete at λ≈0.4, the exact edge where F-minimization and E(S)-generation balance.

self_organization_ca.name: Self Organization CA
self_organization_ca.qfep_connection: Self-organization IS F-minimization made visible — local interactions spontaneously produce global order. The system finds its own low-F configuration without external instruction.

sierpinski_pyramid.description: Recursive Sierpinski Pyramid construction using cubes.
sierpinski_pyramid.name: Sierpinski Pyramid
sierpinski_pyramid.qfep_connection: Fractal self-similarity as infinite F-compression — the same pattern at every scale. Sierpinski's triangle emerges from Rule 90 (a CA), showing how recursive structure achieves maximum order with minimum description length.

fold_theatre_runner.description: F-edge first cycle. Substrate runner subclass with all four channels enabled — visibility cycles rule_30 / sierpinski / menger_sponge (the fold vocabulary), glyph runs subdivide_by_attention, part tags via flower_grammar, color-by-role paints concentric flower anatomy. PATH_GUARANTEE keeps spawn-to-teleporter walkable across every visibility pattern. Used by Fold_Theatre in qfeplaboratory.
fold_theatre_runner.name: Fold Theatre Runner

grid_substrate_runner.description: Integrated substrate component — single-cell artifact that mounts visibility (and optionally colour) mutators on the MAP'S existing GridMultiMesh. Same integration shape as gridcolorizer: doesn't build its own multimesh, finds the floor that's already there. Cycles Wolfram CA, fractal, and BFS-frontier expressions on the actual cubes the player walks. Floor-plan SPAWN_LARGEST keeps reachability honest.
grid_substrate_runner.name: Grid Substrate Runner

volumetric_fog_ca.description: 3D Cellular Automata driving a volumetric fog.
volumetric_fog_ca.name: Volumetric Fog CA

wireworld_circuit.description: Wireworld cellular automaton — 4-state CA for logic gates and signal routing. Displays an OR gate with clock inputs on a floor display, demonstrating how simple state-transition rules produce computational behavior.
wireworld_circuit.name: Wireworld Circuit
wireworld_circuit.qfep_connection: Computation as signal propagation through constraint — pure F-minimization in a cellular medium. Electrons flow through wire topology; the circuit IS the F-model that channels E(S).

ca_conway_city.name: Conway Emergent City
ca_conway_city.description: Walkable modernist skyline emerging from Conway's Game of Life. B=[3], S=[2,3] run for 10 steps; surviving cells become cubes, height driven by live-neighbor count. No urban planner — the rule is the architect. Change the rule string and the city becomes a different kind of thing.

ca_rule_comparison.name: CA Rule Comparison Garden
ca_rule_comparison.description: Five mini-cities arranged in a cross, each running the same initial density+seed through a different CA rule: Conway B3/S23, HighLife B36/S23, Seeds B2/S, Day-and-Night B3678/S34678, Life-without-Death B3/S012345678. Walking between them teaches rule-sensitivity: the seed is identical, only the acceptance function changed, and the cities are entirely different.
